paper.title: Metabolomic machine learning predictor for diagnosis and prognosis of gastric cancer

claims.text: Targeted LC-MS metabolomics of 702 plasma samples (389 GC, 313 NGC) reveals GC metabolic reprogramming; 45 metabolites differ between GC and NGC (Wilcoxon, FDR<0.05, FC>1.25 or <0.8).
claims.location: Abstract; Results 'Reprogrammed plasma metabolic landscape'; Methods 'Metabolic differential analysis'

claims.text: A 10-metabolite random-forest diagnostic model (10-DM) reaches AUROC 0.967 (95% CI 0.944-0.987), sensitivity 0.854, specificity 0.926 in test set 1.
claims.location: Results 'Biomarker panel derived from machine learning'; Fig. 3b

claims.text: The 10-DM model validates in an external test set (Cohort 2) with AUROC 0.920, sensitivity 0.905, specificity 0.75.

The 10-DM model detects early-stage GC: stage IA accuracy 90.9% (AUROC 0.957, sens 0.813, spec 0.926) and stage IB accuracy 0.927 (AUROC 0.984, sens 1, spec 0.926) in test set 1; stage IA accuracy 79.1% (AUROC 0.909) in test set 2.
The 10-DM model outperforms the conventional 3-biomarker panel (CA19-9, CA72-4, CEA): sensitivity 0.925 vs 0.428 (any-of-three rule); single-marker sensitivities 0.217/0.317/0.165.
claims.location: Results 'Comparison of the diagnostic performance'; Supplementary Fig. 4a,b

claims.text: The 10-DM model outperforms SVM, logistic regression, random forest and PLS-DA models built in MetaboAnalyst.
A 28-metabolite random-survival-forest prognostic model (28-PM) reaches c-index 0.90 in training and c-index 0.83 / AUROC 0.832 (95% CI 0.697-0.951) in the test set.
claims.location: Results 'The metabolic prognostic model'; Fig. 4a,b; Methods 'Prognostic model'

claims.text: The 28-PM model outperforms clinical parameters (TNM staging, macroscopic appearance, vascular tumor embolus) and adding clinical parameters yields only a 1% benefit.
claims.location: Results 'The addition of clinical parameters'; Fig. 4d; Supplementary Fig. 5c

claims.text: The 28-PM risk score (cutoff 2.1) stratifies patients into high- and low-risk groups with different OS/DFS, and is an independent prognostic factor in multivariate Cox regression (HR 7.53, 95% CI 2.83-20.04).
Eleven of the 28 prognostic metabolites individually distinguish overall survival in the test set.

findings.location: Methods 'Diagnostic prediction model' vs code/GC-diagnosis-model/run.ipynb cell 5
findings.evidence: Methods: 'We set the coefficient of the L1 constraint as 0.01'. Code: ArgsClass(k=10, alpha=0.005) passed to Selection -> Lasso(alpha=0.005, normalize=True, max_iter=10000) (model.py, fit()). The released run therefore used alpha=0.005, not 0.01.
findings.question_for_authors: Which L1 coefficient produced the reported 10-metabolite panel: 0.01 as stated in the Methods, or 0.005 as in the released notebook?

findings.evidence: Claim 'The 10-DM diagnostic model reaches AUROC >= 0.90 in test set 1 and the 28-PM prognostic model reaches a test c-index >= 0.80' holds in 33% of 24 universes. Single changes that flip it: seed=2; prog_selection=train.
findings.question_for_authors: Was the result checked under seed=2; prog_selection=train?

findings.evidence: The paper reports "95% confidence" intervals, but the code computes the interval with 5%/95% bounds (`confidence_lower = sorted_scores[int(0.05 * len(sorted_scores))]`) (and 1 similar line(s)), which is a 90% interval; no 2.5%/97.5% bounds appear anywhere in the code. Check whether the reported intervals are 90% intervals.
findings.question_for_authors: Are the reported confidence intervals 95% or 90% intervals?

findings.evidence: The paper names Cox regression ("…nical parameters with significant prognostic relevance identified by univariate Cox regression analysis. Parameters with a P < 0.05 were considered statistically s…"), but no matching call (/coxph|CoxPH|lifelines/) was found outside comments in 7 code file(s).
findings.question_for_authors: Where in the released code is the Cox regression performed?

findings.question_for_authors: Was any model, selector or importance estimate fitted on the test set?

findings.evidence: Loop at code cell 9 line 5 refits a model for each value of a setting and scores every candidate on test-named data (code cell 9 line 17). If the reported setting was picked from this sweep, the test set was used for model selection and its score is optimistic.
findings.question_for_authors: How was the reported setting chosen: on training/validation data or on the test set?

findings.evidence: The 3-biomarker comparison uses 208 GC patients (Biomarker_clinical.xlsx, all rows state=1; cohorts cohort2 61, cohort3 84, cohort4 63) and no NGC controls, so only sensitivity can be computed and no specificity or AUROC is reported for CA19-9/CA72-4/CEA. The 10-DM sensitivity of 0.925 is quoted for the same 208 patients, but the released prediction scores cover only 142 (test set 1) + 95 (external test set 2) = 237 samples, of which 111 are GC; the source of the 0.925 value is not released.
findings.question_for_authors: Which samples and which model output produced the 10-DM sensitivity of 0.925 in the biomarker comparison, and were control samples available for the three protein markers?

findings.evidence: Stage labels mix two coding schemes: cohort_information.xlsx contains 'I' (42 rows) as well as 'IA' (56) and 'IB' (11), and the released prediction files contain 'I' rows with no IA/IB label (test set 1: 0 GC in stage 'I'; external test set 2: 0 GC in stage 'I'). The stage IA/IB analyses therefore use only the subset with sub-stage labels (test set 1: 16 IA, 2 IB; test set 2: 11 IA, 4 IB), and the stage IB sensitivity of 1.0 rests on 2 patients.
findings.question_for_authors: How were stage I patients without an IA/IB sub-stage label handled in the stage-specific analyses, and how many stage IB patients were available?

findings.location: Methods 'Patients, data collection, and study design'; data/GC-diagnosis-model/discovery_set.xlsx
findings.evidence: Batch is fully confounded with class in Cohort 1: batch1 contains 118 NGC and 0 GC, batch2 110 NGC and 61 GC, batch3 53 NGC and 84 GC (discovery_set.xlsx). The Methods describe QC-based batch normalisation but no batch adjustment is applied before the differential analysis or the models, and the discovery/test split is drawn within batch, so batch composition differs between the two sets.
findings.question_for_authors: How was the batch/class confounding in Cohort 1 handled, and does the 10-DM model performance depend on batch composition?

findings.location: Methods 'Diagnostic prediction model' vs code/GC-diagnosis-model/run.ipynb cell 5
findings.evidence: Methods: 'selected ten features with nonzero coefficients based on the misclassification error averaged from 10,000 times of random cross-validation'. Code: 10,000 independent StratifiedShuffleSplit draws (test_size=0.33, random_state=i), each followed by a single Lasso fit on the whole training split; the ten features are the ten most frequently selected indices (Counts.most_common()). No cross-validation and no misclassification error is computed.
findings.question_for_authors: Was the feature selection a 10,000-repeat cross-validation on misclassification error, or the 10,000 random-split frequency count implemented in the notebook?

findings.location: Methods 'Diagnostic prediction model' vs code/GC-diagnosis-model/run.ipynb cell 5
findings.evidence: Methods: 'The participants (Cohort 1, n = 426) were randomly stratified sampling into a discovery dataset (n = 284) and a test set (n = 142)'. Code: the 284/142 split is drawn separately inside each of the three batches (batch1 118, batch2 171, batch3 137) and then concatenated, so the split is stratified by batch as well as by class; the released Xtrain/Xtest files are one such draw.
findings.question_for_authors: Was the discovery/test split stratified by batch (as in the code) or only by class (as in the Methods)?

findings.location: Methods 'Diagnostic prediction model' vs code/GC-diagnosis-model/run.ipynb cell 5
findings.evidence: The code excludes four metabolites from the candidate features because of poor peak shapes ('Glycerate-2P_Glycerate-3P_neg-006','Citraconic acid_neg-025','Pyridoxine_pos-137','Argininosuccinic acid_pos-039'). The Methods do not mention this exclusion, although it changes the feature pool from 147 to 143 metabolites.
findings.question_for_authors: Which metabolites were excluded before feature selection, and on what pre-specified criterion?

findings.location: Methods 'Diagnostic prediction model' and 'Prognostic model' vs environment/Dockerfile
findings.evidence: Methods: scikit-learn v.0.24.1 and scikit-survival v.0.17.1. Dockerfile: scikit-learn==1.0.2 and scikit-survival==0.17.0. The released environment therefore differs from the versions named in the paper.
findings.question_for_authors: Which package versions produced the reported numbers?

findings.evidence: Methods: 'A random survival forest (RSF) model comprising 1000 trees was trained to select prominent features according to their permutation-based feature importance.' Code: the 1000-tree RSF is fitted on Xtrain, but PermutationImportance is fitted on the TEST set (perm.fit(Xtest, ytest), cell 7), and the number of retained features (28) is chosen by sweeping 1..147 features and reading the test-set c-index (cell 9).
findings.question_for_authors: Were the permutation importances and the choice of 28 features computed on the training set or on the test set?

findings.evidence: Methods: the 28-PM model has 'great predictive power (AUROC = 0.832, 95% Cl: 0.697-0.951)'. Code cell 12 prints 'testing data c-index: 0.826087' for the 28-feature model; the 0.832 AUROC is computed in cell 17 from the same risk scores. The paper reports the c-index as 0.83 and the AUROC as 0.832, i.e. two different metrics on the same 60 patients.
findings.question_for_authors: Which metric is the headline test-set performance of the 28-PM model, the c-index (0.83) or the AUROC (0.832)?

findings.location: Fig. 3b and Fig. 4b legends vs code/GC-diagnosis-model/run.ipynb cell 8 and code/GC-prognosis-model/run.ipynb cell 16
findings.evidence: Legends: 'A 95% confidence interval was calculated based on the mean and covariance of one thousand random sampling tests'. Code: the CI function takes the 5th and 95th percentiles of 1,000 bootstrap AUROCs (confidence_lower = sorted_scores[int(0.05*len)], confidence_upper = sorted_scores[int(0.95*len)]) and its own comment says 'Computing the lower and upper bound of the 90% confidence interval'. No mean/covariance is used.
findings.question_for_authors: Are the reported AUROC intervals 95% or 90% intervals, and were they computed from percentiles or from a mean/covariance approximation?

findings.evidence: Methods: 'The best cutoff was 2.1, determined by the highest true positive rate (0.9) together with the lowest false positive rate (0.3)'. Code: the cutoff is a hard-coded constant (2.1026 in code/GC-prognosis-model/Rscript/model_prediction_performance.R); no search over cutoffs appears in the released code, and the test set has 10 deaths, so a TPR of 0.9 corresponds to 9 of 10 deaths.
findings.question_for_authors: On which sample was the 2.1 cutoff chosen, and was it chosen before or after looking at the test-set outcomes?
